title: Bigfoot in Pennsylvania? Here's where PA ranks for sightings of the famous beast

content:
(WTAJ) — For centuries, people across the globe have reported seeing Bigfoot, but where does Pennsylvania rank for sightings?

Canada Sports Betting analyzed data across the United States and more than a dozen Canadian Provinces to compile a list of Bigfoot sightings per 100,000 people.

The top of the list is dominated by the Pacific Northwest and includes Washington with 9.17 reported sightings per 100,000 people, Oregon at 6.13, and Idaho at 5.27.

The Northwest (Washington, mainly) was home to lovable bigfoot Harry from the ’80s family comedy “Harry and the Hendersons.”

Moving to the East Coast, Pennsylvania ranks number 28 with 1.01 reported sightings per 100,000 people. The number comes from data collected by the BFRO (Bigfoot Field Researchers Organization) and analyzed by Canada Sports Betting.

Pennsylvania has implied spotting odds of 1.59%, with roughly 59% of the Commonwealth covered in forest. Inside Pennsylvania, the report shows that Pittsburgh has 1.16 sightings per 100,000, while Philadelphia has 0.44 sightings per.

The top ten chart can be seen below.

Canada Sports Betting said the rankings include all 50 U.S. states and 13 Canadian provinces and territories.

So whether you call it Bigfoot or Sasquatch, the truth may still be out there hiding in Pennsylvania.
